doc.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009

title: No personality clashes in the band
summary: No disputes at Hamilton or in the Federal Jazz Commission.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Did you ever have personality clashes in the band?

I know. And the same thing has held true in the band that I’ve been most recently associated with in Washington, the Federal Jazz Commission. There has never been, to my knowledge, any kind of open dispute really about anything. And of course I’m just a sideman and I have known the leader for many, many years and worked in the band 18 years, but he had that band for I guess 30, so I don’t know all of the history of all of that, but generally speaking at Hamilton no there wasn’t any problem. Unless somebody couldn’t make a gig, which happened. And then there was no animosity about it. I can’t make it. I either got another gig or I’ve got class or something.
